We offer a full range of services—from cleanings and cosmetic treatments to crowns, implants, and root canals—using advanced technology. Whether you need routine or urgent care, we’re here for your smile!

We accept ALL PPO insurance plans. We do not accept HMO or Medicaid insurances. We offer a variety of financial assistance programs, as well as our in-house savings plan iSmile.

Call to connect with our team during business hours, or call us after hours to book appointments with our virtual support team, available 24/7. Prefer to book online? Schedule anytime through our website or Google page. New patients welcome!

[{"id": "5074786379954134344", "text": "What you do in the first 24 hours after a tooth extraction directly affects how fast you heal.
Bite down gently on the gauze provided. Avoid spitting forcefully, rinsing with pressure, or using a straw — these create suction that can dislodge the blood clot and lead to dry socket. Keep your head elevated and rest as much as possible.
Some swelling, mild soreness, and light bleeding are all normal during this window. The clot forming in the socket is doing essential work protecting the underlying tissue and bone.
At Dental Group of Chicago, the team who performed your extraction guides your recovery. We're open Monday through Friday 8am–8pm and on Saturdays, so you can always reach us when questions come up.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipOH8VvrWq3M-3xqGYjIAKbK-46DUF9St2P8TDHb=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": "Call now", "posted_at": "2026-07-07T16:21:36", "expires_at": "2027-01-06T16:21:35", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "7046268375950681644", "text": "Dental pain has a way of striking at the most inconvenient times; often late at night, on weekends, or during holidays when your dentist’s office is closed. If you’re experiencing tooth pain after hours, you’re likely wondering whether to seek immediate care or wait until morning. Understanding when dental pain requires urgent attention can help you avoid unnecessary discomfort and make informed decisions about your oral health.

At Dental Group of Chicago, we understand that dental emergencies don’t follow a 9-to-5 schedule. That’s why we’re here to help guide you through these situations and provide the after-hours care you need. We know how stressful dental pain can be, especially when it happens outside regular business hours, and we want to ensure you get the relief you deserve.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipMGqOKPwY2QEb7S47CGOozSc-0CzRPXr5dyUT-v=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://dentalgroupofchicago.com/after-hours-dental-pain-guide/", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2025-09-10T13:15:45", "expires_at": "2026-03-12T13:15:44", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "2547641146412441261", "text": "Every day, thousands of Chicago residents make important decisions about their oral health, yet many remain unaware of how their choices compare to regional trends and national benchmarks. The latest data from authoritative sources, including the CDC’s 2024 Oral Health Surveillance Report and the American Dental Association’s Health Policy Institute, reveal compelling insights about dental health patterns across our region, painting a picture of both challenges and opportunities for improving community wellness.

At Dental Group of Chicago, we see these statistics come to life in our South Loop practice, where we serve patients from across the greater Chicagoland area. Because of this, we strive to deliver comprehensive general dentistry services designed to address the most common oral health concerns affecting our community. Understanding these regional patterns helps us provide better care and helps you make informed decisions about your dental health.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipPJ6AHnkDX5zZ9XQCLSY1olaLbghY6T3OdUULS6=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://dentalgroupofchicago.com/chicago-dental-health-statistics/", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2025-09-10T13:15:05", "expires_at": "2026-03-12T13:15:04", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "7698461488549875575", "text": "New Patient Special: Get an initial cleaning, comprehensive exam, and a full set of digital X-rays for only $99. Perfect for new patients without insurance. Schedule your appointment today at Dental Group of Chicago!", "type": "offer", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipMmaUmyNZA1a24BHY_2H4pueWQS4alvpZPtCivT=h400-no", "title": "New Patient Promotion", "cta_url": "https://search.google.com/local/posts?q=Dental+Group+of+Chicago+Family+%26+Emergency+Dentistry&ludocid=12220838318085764726&lpsid=7698461488549875575&source=sh/x/loc/post&lsig=AB86z5UNSkE527XZKIi76dqh0Z38", "cta_label": "View Offer", "posted_at": "2025-08-11T19:33:33", "expires_at": "2025-09-30T22:00:00", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "5492451811653278184", "text": "Invisalign® straightens your teeth just as effectively as traditional metal braces but instead uses a modern approach that is best suited for an active and social lifestyle. The clear plastic aligners are virtually invisible, so no one has to know they are there. And unlike traditional braces, the invisible aligners are removable! This makes it possible to brush and floss your teeth without the interference of brackets that can contribute to tooth decay. You can pop these invisible braces out to eat and drink whatever you like with no food restrictions. 

Traditional braces use wires and metal that can poke and irritate your gums, but Invisalign® is made of smooth plastic that is comfortable to wear. The convenience of this South Loop, Chicago Invisalign® treatment is that it appeals to people in all stages of life. Schedule a consultation with the Dental Group of Chicago if you are ready to improve your smile.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipNvIBdeqizbZUTVTGfKLWWtdMWL3GNHYTtiihg1=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://dentalgroupofchicago.com/invisalign/", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2025-06-18T19:50:57", "expires_at": "2025-12-18T19:50:56", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "9223017403217784985", "text": "Dental anxiety affects many people, making a simple check-up feel like a nerve-wracking experience. Research shows that 50-80% of adults in the U.S. suffer to some degree of dental anxiety, with about 12% experiencing extreme fear that can cause them to avoid seeking dental care altogether. This type of anxiety can be triggered by several factors, including fear of pain, past negative experiences, or simply the unknown of what a dental visit might involve.

At the Dental Group of Chicago, we understand how anxiety can prevent individuals from receiving the necessary care. Our team goes above and beyond to ensure you feel comfortable and relaxed during your visit. We provide a range of techniques and support to make every dental appointment as stress-free as possible.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipNmpADkQC8MktGvJYiJxUte7zexHAJIi7RDIL5f=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://dentalgroupofchicago.com/dental-anxiety-heres-how-we-ensure-your-comfort-during-dental-procedure/", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2025-06-18T19:48:51", "expires_at": "2025-12-18T19:48:50", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "7606818636776178612", "text": "When your dentist tells you you need a dental crown, several questions may immediately flood your mind. Will it look natural? How long will it last? Can I afford the procedure? With modern dentistry offering everything from traditional gold to cutting-edge zirconia, finding your ideal crown match becomes a balance between aesthetics, durability, and cost. The perfect crown for your specific situation depends not just on the tooth’s location but also on your lifestyle, budget, and smile goals.

At Dental Group of Chicago, we provide comprehensive crown services to help restore your smile’s functionality and appearance. Our team is committed to delivering accessible dental care with extended hours from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Monday through Friday and Saturday appointments. This ensures even the busiest patients can receive the necessary preventative and restorative care.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipOMM4c9jBp46ciDIf08ZpK-58KV2Ee_k2rGXFdm=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://dentalgroupofchicago.com/types-of-dental-crowns/", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2025-06-18T19:47:42", "expires_at": "2025-12-18T19:47:41", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "6570429578350112205", "text": "Having a beautiful smile may be even easier than you think. Many people achieve the look they’ve been dreaming of with our simple “bleaching” procedure.

Teeth whitening is safe, quick, and inexpensive. Just let us know at any appointment if you would like to whiten your teeth. You can lighten only your upper teeth or both the upper and lower, depending on how much you show when you talk and smile.

In only a day or two your custom bleach splints will be ready for you to pick up. We provide you with a special bleaching agent that you put into the clear splints. With only a few hours of wear per day, our special bleaching agent bubbles stains right out of your enamel in a very short time without altering tooth structure or existing dental work in any way. When your teeth reach the desired brightness, only occasional treatment is needed to maintain your new smile. We’ll want to take “after” photos at your next appointment.

[{"id": "4639547202384823078", "text": "Losing a tooth changes more than the way your smile looks. Under the gap, the jawbone that once supported the tooth root begins to change, too.

A natural tooth root does more than anchor a tooth in place. It transfers the force of chewing into the surrounding jawbone, and that steady pressure helps keep the bone active. Once the root is gone, the bone receives less stimulation and begins to remodel, often without any pain or warning sign.

This article explains why that happens, how quickly changes can begin, what happens when several teeth are missing, and how dental implants in Chicago differ from removable options like bridges and dentures at the bone level. If you are missing a tooth or thinking ahead about missing teeth in Chicago, understanding this process before exploring dental implants in Wicker Park can help you make a more informed decision about timing and treatment.

Why Does the Jawbone Shrink After a Tooth Is Lost?
The jawbone that once held a tooth in place is called the alveolar ridge. This ridge relies partly on the presence of a tooth root and the forces of chewing to maintain its shape and density.

It helps to think of this as remodeling rather than disappearing. The body is not losing bone randomly. It is adjusting bone structure because the functional demand that used to be there, the pressure from a tooth root during chewing, is no longer present.

", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipPAXvE3AuWQlPzozNNwooPv6vXEgMdOcXH-Ybxu=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://www.smilesciencechicago.com/jawbone-loss-after-tooth-loss-guide-dental-implants-chicago/", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-09-04T11:48:05", "expires_at": "2027-03-06T11:48:04", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "5924567628647601930", "text": "Planning a dental implant used to happen mostly in the dentist’s head, based on X-rays and experience. Today, much of that planning happens digitally, before a patient ever sits in the surgical chair.

A dental implant surgical guide is the tool that connects that digital plan to the actual procedure. It is a custom device designed to help transfer a planned implant position into the mouth during surgery. A guide can help direct the location, angle, and depth of the implant, along with its relationship to the future crown.

A guide adds a helpful layer of control. It does not replace the dentist’s clinical judgment, training, or hands-on decision-making during surgery. This article explains what a surgical guide is, how Smile Science Chicago creates one, and what it can and cannot do for patients considering dental implants in Wicker Park and across Chicago.

What Is a Dental Implant Surgical Guide?
A dental implant surgical guide is a custom-fabricated device made specifically for one patient’s mouth. It fits over the teeth, gums, or another stable structure, and it contains openings, often called sleeves, positioned according to a pre-approved digital plan.

During surgery, these openings help direct drills and other instruments toward predetermined positions. The guide does not perform the surgery. It supports the dentist’s hands by marking out where the plan says each implant should go.

", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipNJhjYhy3p93Xe06AEgdkLdnZl4uUEk0u3w49f5=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://www.smilesciencechicago.com/dental-implant-surgical-guides-accuracy-wicker-park-il/", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-09-04T11:47:46", "expires_at": "2027-03-06T11:47:45", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "5794155871965028211", "text": "Many people call the visible tooth an implant, but that visible tooth is actually only one part of a complete restoration. A full dental implant restoration is made up of three separate components working together: the implant itself, a connector called an abutment, and a crown on top.

Understanding these three parts helps you know what to expect before, during, and after treatment. It also explains why dental implants in Chicago often involve several appointments rather than one visit. Whether you’re researching dental implants in Wicker Park or exploring implant dentistry in Chicago more broadly, this guide breaks down each component so you can walk into a consultation with realistic expectations.

What Is a Dental Implant? Understanding the Part That Replaces Your Tooth Root
The implant itself is not the tooth you see when you smile. It is a small post placed inside the jawbone, and its job is to replace the root of a missing tooth rather than the crown of the tooth.

Once in place, the implant supports chewing forces, helps preserve the jawbone, and maintains the shape of the face by keeping bone tissue active. Without a root or an implant in its place, the jawbone in that area can begin to lose density over time.

data.description:
For 40 years, Chicago Dental 312 has provided ethical, high-quality dental care in the heart of the Chicago Loop. Our general dentistry practice offers comprehensive care, from cleanings, exams, and fillings to dental implants, Invisalign, veneers, crowns, root canals and teeth whitening. Whether it's a simple checkup or a full smile makeover, we stay current on the latest technology and give honest advice so you can make the decisions that are right for your oral health.

Our dental procedures are second to none. We have dental implant providers that perform:

Single Tooth Replacement
Anterior Replacement
Posterior Replacement
Full Upper Replacement
Veneers

Dental implants are one of the most popular choices for replacing missing teeth.

Welcome to the office of Chicago dentist, Dr. Ankita Shah! As the owner of our well established and reputable dental practice in the West Loop Chicago, Dr. Shah is excited to invite patients to Dental Smiles of West Loop. Grandson of the practice founder, Dr. Dan Strobel, along with Dr. Isabella Terrassa and their team provide leading-edge dentistry in our Chicago-based dental office. With over 92 years of family operation in the same location, Strobel Dentistry is committed to providing honest, comprehensive care to our patients using the latest technology and industry knowledge in a supportive atmosphere. Our dentists offer various services, including dental implants, veneers, cosmetic dentistry, Invisalign, same-day crowns, dental cleanings, oral sleep appliances, Myofunctional therapy, Solea laser dentistry, and the latest in digital imaging. We are welcoming new patients. Become a part of our family!

[{"id": "5531256970103367322", "text": "Invisalign uses a series of custom-made, removable clear aligners to gradually shift your teeth into alignment. No wires, no brackets, and no food restrictions. For most patients, no one even notices they’re in treatment.

Downtown Chicago Invisalign at Strobel Dentistry is handled entirely in-house by certified providers, from free consultation to retainers at the end.", "type": "event", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipOafjF8g_DQbWxVtTVMy2FrJk7VK_7cn2ciQLWI=h400-no", "title": "Trusted Downtown Chicago Invisalign | Strobel Dentistry", "cta_url": null, "cta_label": "Call now", "posted_at": "2026-08-26T22:52:41", "expires_at": "2026-12-11T05:59:59", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "8228276716225601242", "text": "Guided Biofilm Therapy (GBT) changes the order of operations on a dental cleaning. A dental cleaning is a procedure that is performed by a dentist or dental hygienist. during a dental cleaning, plaque and tartar are removed from the teeth. The teeth are then polished and flossed. 

Dental cleanings are important because they help to remove bacteria from the mouth and prevent cavities. 

If you have not had a dental cleaning in a while, be sure to schedule an appointment with your dentist to maintain great oral health.

Learn more about our dental office by visiting our website at ", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipMCRhIaOGfsWuJFqmwDc9GLinivD-d6UN5LVEEc=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2022-10-19T21:33:12", "expires_at": "2023-04-20T21:33:12", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "6336120821925791147", "text": "Dental sedation can help to make dental procedures more comfortable for patients who experience anxiety or fear.

The American Academy of Pediatric Dentistry (AAPD) recommends that children see a dentist by the time they are one year old. This is because dental problems can begin at a young age and it is important to catch them early. 

If you wait until your child is three or four years old, they may already have developed cavities. 

The AAPD also recommends that children have a dental visit every six months. This is because regular dental visits can help to prevent cavities and other problems. 

If you are looking for a dentist for your child, be sure to ask about their experience with young children. You want to make sure that they are comfortable working with kids and that they have a good bedside manner.

Tartar is difficult to remove and it can irritate your gums, which can lead to inflammation. Inflammation can destroy the tissues and bones that support your teeth. 

If you have periodontal disease, you may need to undergo a deep cleaning, which is a type of procedure that removes tartar from below the gum line. You may also need to take medication or have surgery to treat the condition. 

If you think you may have periodontal disease, be sure to see your dentist for an examination. Early diagnosis and treatment is important in order to prevent the progression of the disease.

At Archer Dentistry, our expert team performs root canals to save damaged or infected teeth and prevent extraction. This treatment removes the inflamed pulp from inside the tooth, alleviating pain and protecting your natural tooth.

Watch for signs like persistent tooth pain, sensitivity, or swelling—these could indicate the need for a root canal. Our painless, multi-step procedure involves cleaning and sealing the tooth, with restoration options like fillings or crowns afterward.

Root canals are always better than extractions, as they allow you to keep your natural tooth, preserving your smile and long-term oral health.

Need root canal treatment in Chicago? Call Archer Dentistry today to book your appointment!

For more information about Root Canals, take a look at our blog post!

Teeth cleanings are essential for maintaining good oral and physical health. At Archer Dentistry, our professional cleanings remove plaque and tartar buildup, preventing gum disease, cavities, and bad breath. Regular cleanings are especially important for those prone to gum disease, with visits recommended every 3-4 months, while others may only need bi-annual cleanings.

During the cleaning, our team uses advanced tools to thoroughly remove plaque, followed by polishing to keep your teeth clean and healthy. After the procedure, you may experience temporary sensitivity, but this will subside quickly.

Delaying cleanings can lead to serious issues like tooth loss due to advanced gum disease. But don’t worry—regular cleanings by our skilled dentists will protect your smile without damaging your teeth!

Ready to schedule your next cleaning? Call Archer Dentistry today to book your appointment! For more information regarding Cleanings, take a look at our recent blog post!

[{"id": "5114635168184521908", "text": "A Healthy Aging Check-In

Healthy Aging Month is a good reminder that changes in the mouth can reveal when an older loved one may need extra support. Use the M.O.U.T.H. checklist:

M — Meals: Are they avoiding certain foods, chewing on one side or taking longer to eat?

O — Ongoing symptoms: Watch for bleeding gums, persistent bad breath, sores, swelling or dry mouth.

U — Unusual behavior: Are they speaking less, resisting brushing or avoiding smiling and socializing?

T — Teeth and dentures: Look for loose or painful teeth, or dentures that click, slip, crack or cause sore spots.

H — Health and medications: Note changes in overall health, medications, memory, mobility or blood glucose.

If something seems different, the team at Aspen Dental can help identify the cause and recommend the right next step.

Led by Dr. Grace Lee, our team offers a full range of services—from preventive care and cosmetic treatments to implants, orthodontics, and TMJ therapy—all in one convenient location. We use cutting-edge tools like CBCT scanning, iTero digital impressions, laser dentistry, and 3D X-rays to ensure precise, comfortable treatments. With flexible financing, multilingual staff, and Saturday appointments, we make exceptional dental care accessible to every smile.

Located in historic Willoughby Tower directly across from Chicago’s beautiful Millennium Park. Our doctors are highly skilled in Cosmetic Dentistry, General Dentistry, Implant Dentistry, and Invisalign. Our commitment is to provide you with excellent care, advanced technology, and a superb patient experience.

[{"id": "7461301180658778905", "text": "Missing teeth can affect your lifestyle and confidence. If you're looking for solutions, dentures and partials may be the answer. At Chicago Dental Dream Team, we provide personalized care, working closely with each patient to find the best denture option. Dentures are designed to replace missing teeth, enhancing appearance and improving chewing and speaking abilities. Partial dentures fit securely with remaining teeth, offering a comfortable solution for oral health. Many patients experience a boost in confidence post-treatment, feeling rejuvenated in social situations without the worry of missing teeth. In addition to aesthetics, dentures help maintain jaw structure and prevent bone loss. Located at 820 East 87th Street Suite 201, Chicago, IL, our experienced team offers comprehensive consultations on various denture types, including conventional and immediate options. We prioritize your comfort and satisfaction, ensuring a smooth journey to restored oral health. Patients appreciate our quality care, with one saying, "The team is incredible! I never dreamed I could feel this good about my smile again." Dentures enhance functionality, allowing you to enjoy a wider variety of foods. With proper care and regular check-ups, you can keep your dentures in excellent condition. For more information on denture services or general dentistry options, visit Chicago Dental Dream Team. Ready to restore your smile?", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipNtixIjWzncY0_wtz__9wIJUOF2dKBTbIioaRFj=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://dentaldreamteam.com/", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-09-21T13:39:17", "expires_at": "2027-03-23T13:39:15", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "7249228144487618848", "text": "Missing teeth can impact not only your smile but also your oral health. [{"id": "4360634938804193432", "text": "Broken or Damaged Tooth? When Might You Need a Same-Day Crown?

A cracked or broken tooth can happen suddenly, sometimes from biting something hard or because an old filling has weakened the tooth.

In many cases, the tooth may still be restored with a crown instead of being removed.

A same-day crown may be considered if:

• Part of the tooth has broken off
• A large filling has weakened the tooth
• The tooth is cracked or badly worn
• The tooth needs extra protection after treatment

If enough healthy tooth structure remains, your dentist may be able to design and place the crown during the same visit.

Not every damaged tooth is suitable for a same-day crown, so an examination is important before treatment is recommended.

Contact our dental team to have your tooth checked and discuss whether a same-day crown may be right for you.
", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipPCX27qylzlB2SCBhIPiERDTB6lsVNuwtRGU2JZ=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": "Call now", "posted_at": "2026-09-03T05:30:00", "expires_at": "2027-03-03T11:21:10", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "4400852150169620709", "text": "Dental bonding vs veneers: which option is right for your smile?

Both treatments can improve the look of chipped, stained, uneven, or slightly gapped teeth, but they are not the same. Dental bonding is often used for smaller cosmetic fixes, while veneers may be recommended for a more complete smile transformation.

Dental bonding may help with:

• Small chips or cracks
• Minor gaps between teeth
• Slight tooth reshaping
• Small areas of discoloration
• A more conservative cosmetic option

Veneers may help with:

• Multiple visible smile concerns
• Stubborn stains that do not respond to whitening
• Worn, uneven, or misshapen teeth
• A longer-lasting smile makeover option
• A more uniform smile appearance

The right choice depends on your tooth condition, smile goals, budget, and oral health. A dental evaluation can help you compare both options and choose the treatment that fits your smile best.

Schedule your cosmetic dentistry consultation today.
", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipPqAFLbrTvD_KZcvd63AqF3P2U_dbpXE_TJwSC3=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://www.datmp.com/services/dental-bonding", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-09-02T19:00:00", "expires_at": "2027-03-03T11:06:27", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "8744688348103117918", "text": "Can Invisalign fix crowded or crooked teeth in adults?

Yes, Invisalign may help many adults improve mild to moderate crowding, crooked teeth, gaps, and alignment concerns without traditional metal braces. These clear aligners are removable, discreet, and designed to gradually move teeth into better positions.

Invisalign may be a good option if you have:

• Crowded front teeth
• Crooked or overlapping teeth
• Small gaps between teeth
• Teeth that shifted after braces
• Mild bite alignment concerns
• A desire for a more discreet orthodontic option

However, not every case is the same. Severe crowding, complex bite problems, or gum health concerns may require a different treatment plan. A dental evaluation can help determine whether Invisalign is suitable for your smile goals.

Our El Paso dental team can examine your teeth, review your bite, and explain your clear aligner options.

Schedule your Invisalign consultation today.

Could Teeth Grinding Be the Cause?

Many people clench or grind their teeth at night without knowing it. 
Over time, this pressure can affect your teeth, jaw muscles, and bite.

Common signs of teeth grinding may include:

• Morning jaw pain or tightness
• Frequent headaches
• Tooth sensitivity
• Worn, chipped, or cracked teeth
• Sore facial muscles
• Pain when chewing
• Clicking or discomfort in the jaw

A custom nightguard may help protect your teeth from grinding damage and reduce pressure on the jaw while you sleep. Your dentist can check for signs of bruxism and recommend the right option based on your symptoms.

Do not ignore ongoing jaw pain or morning headaches. Early care can help protect your smile and prevent further tooth damage.

Schedule a teeth grinding evaluation today.

[{"id": "2237837104680352447", "text": "
Caption: Mouthwash can leave your mouth feeling fresh, but it's not a shortcut to a healthy smile. Brushing, flossing, and regular dental checkups work together to keep your teeth and gums in great shape.

Do you use mouthwash every day? We'd love to know what's part of your daily routine! 👇

📞 Always There Dental Care is here to help you build healthy habits for a lifetime of smiles. Book your next visit today.

", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipOyGN0e39GKypc9lj74m_ofvN9zkLRBz8xnPJCL=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": "Call now", "posted_at": "2026-09-19T08:37:28", "expires_at": "2027-03-21T08:37:27", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "346864972048969068", "text": "What Happens When a Tooth Is Too Damaged to Save?

A cracked or badly broken tooth can be stressful, especially when you're unsure whether it can still be repaired. The answer depends on factors such as how much healthy tooth structure remains, where the damage is located, and whether the tooth can be predictably restored.

Depending on the situation, treatment could include a filling, crown, root canal treatment, or tooth extraction. If the damage is too extensive for predictable restoration, extraction may be recommended.

Don't try to determine the severity of a damaged tooth on your own. An examination allows your dentist to assess the problem and discuss your options.

At Always There Dental Care, we can evaluate damaged or painful teeth and help you understand the next step. If you're concerned about a broken or severely damaged tooth, contact our team for an appointment.
", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipMNJMJn7ImQTfx_R1G8cmAd7a0UVUoFL7i-1pLG=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": "Call now", "posted_at": "2026-09-18T08:33:05", "expires_at": "2027-03-20T08:33:02", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "633267605928555047", "text": "Why Do Wisdom Teeth Sometimes Need to Be Removed?

Wisdom teeth don't automatically need to be removed simply because they are present. However, wisdom tooth removal may be recommended when these teeth cause problems or are likely to create complications.

Common reasons for considering removal include:

A wisdom tooth is impacted or unable to erupt properly
Repeated inflammation around the tooth
Tooth decay that is difficult to treat
Damage to an adjacent tooth
Gum problems around the wisdom tooth
Limited space that contributes to other dental concerns

The decision should be based on an examination and, when appropriate, dental imaging. Your dentist can explain whether monitoring or removal is the better option for your situation.

At Always There Dental Care, we provide personalised guidance for patients considering wisdom tooth removal. Schedule an appointment to discuss your concerns.
", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipPvwMteRN2JbTArbgji5H7d9DHV8GEwOtgSgZir=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": "Call now", "posted_at": "2026-09-15T08:32:06", "expires_at": "2027-03-17T08:32:05", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "3135308857102097611", "text": "Today is National Grandparents Day! Let’s take a moment to appreciate the love and support that grandparents bring to our lives. 💛

These wise family members take on many different names, depending on family traditions and cultures. Whether it’s Grandma, Grandpa, Nana, Papa, Gigi, Mimi, or Yiayia- we’d love to hear what your favorite grandparent nicknames are in the comments! 

📞 Always There Dental Care is honored to care for smiles across generations. Schedule your family's next dental visit today.

", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipOH5BCAi01Iv1VxKZwIgkEU-yvhllHwyzbsrtBm=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": "Call now", "posted_at": "2026-09-13T08:09:45", "expires_at": "2027-03-15T08:09:44", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "1049434994283005307", "text": "When Is Tooth Extraction the Right Choice?

Saving a natural tooth is often preferred when it can be restored predictably. However, there are situations where removing a tooth may be the safest or most appropriate option.

A dentist may recommend damaged tooth extraction when a tooth is severely broken, extensively decayed, or otherwise unable to be restored. Extraction may also be considered when a tooth is causing ongoing problems that cannot be managed with other treatments.

Before recommending removal, your dentist can assess the tooth and discuss whether restorative options are possible.

At Always There Dental Care, we take the time to explain why an extraction may be recommended and what you can expect from the procedure. If you're experiencing pain or have a severely damaged tooth, don't wait for the problem to worsen.

Contact Always There Dental Care to schedule an evaluation.
", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipOtqsdmsXFjCYGdKLI24JFkWfs6rZmAUj6CPyZU=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": "Call now", "posted_at": "2026-09-10T08:32:09", "expires_at": "2027-03-12T08:32:07", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "6576394792514130693", "text": "What Should I Do After a Professional Dental Cleaning? 

After a routine dental cleaning, most patients can return to their normal activities immediately. If your teeth have been polished or you received a fluoride treatment, your dental team may provide specific instructions about eating or drinking. It's also normal to experience mild sensitivity, especially if significant tartar was removed or your gums were inflamed before the appointment. Continuing to brush twice a day, floss daily, and drink plenty of water will help maintain the results of your cleaning. Keeping up with regular dental visits is equally important for preventing plaque and tartar from building up again. At Always There Dental Care, we'll provide personalized oral hygiene recommendations to help you maintain a clean, healthy smile between appointments.

", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipM6i_ktFzQuy9BVhLGgZNAfG4ysxwp6GMEgC7Fj=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": "Call now", "posted_at": "2026-08-31T08:32:05", "expires_at": "2027-03-02T08:32:03", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "1950541982477495375", "text": "A small white spot on your tooth may seem harmless, but it can be one of the earliest signs of tooth decay.

Chalky white patches, a rough tooth surface, or increasing sensitivity are all signs that your teeth may need professional attention. Treating these changes early can help prevent cavities from progressing.

Have you ever noticed a small change in your teeth that turned out to be something more? Share your experience in the comments below!

Protect your smile with an early dental evaluation at Always There Dental Care in Chicago, Illinois. Schedule your visit today.

", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipPT2H-mbm8gnA8mJMoMAd_YX13xs8VjzUfWZPlO=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": "Call now", "posted_at": "2026-08-29T08:34:06", "expires_at": "2027-02-28T08:34:05", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "7482604132342672655", "text": "Is a Dental Cleaning Different From a Deep Cleaning? 

Yes. A routine dental cleaning and a deep cleaning are two different procedures designed for different oral health needs. A routine cleaning focuses on removing plaque, tartar, and surface stains from above the gumline to help prevent cavities and gum disease. A deep cleaning, also known as scaling and root planing, is typically recommended when gum disease is present. It involves cleaning below the gumline to remove bacteria and tartar from the tooth roots and help the gums heal. Your dentist will evaluate your teeth and gums during your examination and recommend the most appropriate type of cleaning based on your oral health. At Always There Dental Care, we provide personalized preventive care to help keep your smile healthy and your gums in excellent condition.
", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipNStlqBQlGhr4VbgYr_0OhsxIW5Us30Qs1lCVtv=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": "Call now", "posted_at": "2026-08-27T08:32:10", "expires_at": "2027-02-26T08:32:09", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "6656397033794934271", "text": "Every little tooth is a big reason to smile!

Happy National Tooth Fairy Day from Always There Dental Care in Chicago, Illinois! Today, we're celebrating healthy smiles, childhood milestones, and the magic of great dental habits.

What did the Tooth Fairy leave under your pillow when you lost your first tooth? We'd love to hear your favorite memory in the comments!

Keep your child's smile healthy with regular dental visits at Always There Dental Care. Book an appointment today.

", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipNg_LTSDF-NOKCrbcbOrm1_apuGqYVvIWOCdTkb=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": "Call now", "posted_at": "2026-08-22T08:33:07", "expires_at": "2027-02-21T08:33:05", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "8515878368609264170", "text": "Don't Wait for Tooth Pain to Visit the Dentist

One of the biggest misconceptions about oral health is that you only need to visit the dentist when something hurts. In reality, many dental problems begin without causing noticeable symptoms.

Routine dental cleanings allow your dental team to:

Remove plaque before it causes damage
Identify cavities early
Monitor gum health
Check existing dental work
Provide personalized oral hygiene advice

By catching concerns early, preventive visits often help keep treatment simpler and your smile healthier.
Whether it's been six months or a little longer, scheduling a professional cleaning is an investment in your long-term oral health.

Contact Always There Dental Care today to schedule your dental cleaning and keep your smile healthy, comfortable, and confident.
", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipPGof3GeWFcBb3YBi4LX5PMtTlAncd8gP9ksDAZ=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": "Call now", "posted_at": "2026-08-17T08:32:04", "expires_at": "2027-02-16T08:32:03", "promo_code": null}]

data.description:
Dr. Brittany Dickinson is a cosmetic dentist in Lakeview, Chicago, specializing in natural, undetectable smile enhancements for patients who want to look refined—not overdone. Her work focuses on porcelain veneers and Invisalign, with a highly personalized approach designed to enhance each patient’s features while preserving long-term oral health.
Known for her attention to detail and aesthetic eye, Dr. Dickinson creates results that blend seamlessly and feel effortlessly confident. The practice is also designed for comfort, offering a calming, patient-centered experience with amenities such as aromatherapy, noise-cancelling headphones, Netflix, sedation options, CBD, and weighted blankets.

[{"id": "2804284362261420104", "text": "This is where veneers actually get made.

Not on a computer. Not in an assembly line. On a stone model of your teeth — hand-layered, hand-shaded, hand-finished by a ceramist who has spent years learning how light moves through porcelain.

Each veneer is fired multiple times. Adjusted. Compared to reference photos of your face. Compared to the shade of the tooth next to it. Then adjusted again.

The reason really good veneers look real is because someone did all this work you'll never see.

We work with ceramists who share that standard. It matters. Every step of it matters.

Curious about the process? Click "Learn more" to explore smile design.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipO26FM_sQ-qcauu25r5JosamQM9YmAZ08GDwpBn=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://chicagoaestheticdentistry.com/smile-design-consultation", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-09-23T01:00:00", "expires_at": "2027-03-02T20:39:57", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "7353395132166773435", "text": "The best veneers don't look like veneers.

That sentence is my whole philosophy. If a patient walks out and someone says "wow, your veneers look amazing" — that's not the compliment I'm aiming for.

The compliment I'm aiming for is: "you look really good lately."

Undetectable. Personalized. Conservative with your tooth structure. Designed to age with your face, not fight against it.

Sixteen years of clinical work — most of it cosmetic — has made me more, not less, restrained. The smallest, most considered changes almost always age the best.

If that resonates with how you think about your own face, we'll get along.

Click "Learn more" to explore a smile design consultation.

— Dr. Brittany Dickinson
", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipOROI9ajOk7SQ4kopW9L5QUO9IE-bTzaE78cl7m=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://chicagoaestheticdentistry.com/smile-design-consultation", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-09-18T01:00:00", "expires_at": "2027-03-02T20:39:01", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "5351761920292458458", "text": "Every smile design starts with looking. A lot of looking.

Photos from every angle. Your smile at rest. Your smile mid-laugh. The way your upper lip moves when you say the word "sixty." Small differences in each of these change the shape of the final result.

Cosmetic dentistry gets rushed when the dentist skips this part.

I don't skip it. Not because I'm slow — because this is where the artistry lives. By the time we've decided on the design, the technical part of placing the veneers is the easy step. Your face has already told us what it wants.

If you've been quietly considering this for a while, the consultation is where the real conversation starts.

Click "Learn more."", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipOKzN63iargDG3OCQZl01vir9vC4EB0vWuy4Xof=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://chicagoaestheticdentistry.com/smile-design-consultation", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-09-17T01:00:00", "expires_at": "2027-03-02T20:38:21", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "4277936700148058762", "text": "Smile design isn't done in the operatory.

It's done at a desk. With reference photos. With your face on the screen. With a lot of quiet study before anything is ever prepped.

I spend real time here. Looking at your smile line against your lip shape. Studying tooth proportion against the width of your face. Deciding — with you — where the edges should sit, how much translucency the incisors should show, whether the canines should stay a touch warmer than the centrals so nothing looks flat.

The best cases are the ones where the design decisions are made before the dentistry starts.

That's the difference between a smile that fits, and a smile that just fills the space.

Click "Learn more" to see how the process starts.

— Dr. Brittany Dickinson", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipMQrZm4JXdqqJA1MRqJIP68hn6Bsip_DVaBur6t=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://chicagoaestheticdentistry.com/smile-design-consultation", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-09-16T01:00:00", "expires_at": "2027-03-02T20:37:29", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "3997648824332694184", "text": "Not every smile change starts with braces.

Some patients have already done Invisalign. Some can't fit another two years of orthodontics into their life. Some just want a cleaner, more even smile line without the wait.

For the right case, porcelain veneers can address crowding, rotation, and length in a single planned process — with a preview to see and approve before anything permanent happens.

It's not a shortcut. It's a different tool. And used carefully, on the right patient, it's beautiful.

The best way to know if it's right for you is to sit down and talk it through together — cases, timing, whether veneers even make sense for your bite.

Click "Learn more" to start with a smile design consultation.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipOsAA_jEr2D3-Ep2l26yD852DkgIHlxY-PBJWXH=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://chicagoaestheticdentistry.com/smile-design-consultation", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-09-11T01:00:00", "expires_at": "2027-03-02T20:36:20", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "685098159401782676", "text": "The tilted front tooth. You've made peace with it. You cover it in photos. You've stopped mentioning it out loud.

Then one day someone posts a candid — and you see it again, exactly the way you've always seen it. And you think: maybe now.

Small changes in shape, angle, and proportion can transform a smile without transforming your face. Veneers, done conservatively, do a lot of quiet work.

The result on the right of the frame? That's the smile our patient always felt she had. The alignment just finally matches how she carries herself.

If a small, meaningful change has been on your mind, click "Learn more."", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipOSWq6fmD1DP3brMZMz76xrNCytMuXFbxMbCZ56=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://chicagoaestheticdentistry.com/smile-design-consultation", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2026-09-10T01:00:00", "expires_at": "2027-03-02T20:35:20", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "2495289590268685406", "text": "Teeth age. The edges wear down. The color shifts. The proportions change. Nothing dramatic in any single year — but stack a decade or two together and suddenly the smile in the photo doesn't feel like yours.

This kind of transformation is one of the most rewarding to design. Not because the "before" is a problem. Because there's a real face behind it — someone who deserves to look in the mirror and recognize herself again.

Porcelain veneers, done conservatively, can restore length, brightness, and shape without touching your personality.

You still look like you. Just rested. Just clearly.

That's not what we do.

That's the goal. Undetectable, not "perfect." Designed for your face, your proportions, your life — not a trend.

If that's the kind of change you've been quietly considering, this is a good place to start.

data.description:
Dental Minds in Logan Square Chicago, IL was founded with an educator's mind. We noticed that there were too many situations where the patient wasn't really aware of one's teeth conditions or wasn't sure why certain procedures were done to them in the past. Often times when asked about why a procedure was done, their reply would simply be ""the dentist told me I needed to get it done."" Our goal is to open an office that will focus on patient education, so that every treatment and every diagnosis can be done with patient's full understanding.

To achieve this, we aim to be transparent in all aspects, and we strive to communicate this transparent information as efficiently and compassionately as possible.

At MG Dentistry & Rejuvenation Center, we are happy to work with most types of insurance and we provide reasonably priced, top-quality care, contact us at (312) 236-3633.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipNeUwEUjBYXLQ9Q8t_U2xPQd9OZFBSjVoBgf03X=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://www.mgdentistry.com/", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2023-02-09T13:05:21", "expires_at": "2023-08-11T13:05:20", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "2382916928457407136", "text": "Reality check! It's essential to know the truth about oral health because bad hygiene can lead you down a path towards tooth decay, loss or other complications. So before your next visit with Dr., get some knowledge on how best take care of yourself by learning what are commonly believed dental myths.

", "type": "update", "image": null, "title": null, "cta_url": "https://www.mgdentistry.com/", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2023-01-27T13:08:24", "expires_at": "2023-07-29T13:08:24", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "2766556049102993922", "text": "Nutrition: What You Eat Affects Your Teeth

Cheese, milk, plain yogurt, calcium-fortified tofu, leafy greens and almonds, are foods that may benefit tooth health thanks to their high amounts of calcium and other nutrients they provide. Protein-rich foods like meat, poultry, fish, milk and eggs are the best sources of phosphorus. Both of these minerals play a critical role in dental health, by protecting and rebuilding tooth enamel.

Fruits and vegetables are good choices for a healthy smile since they are high in water and fiber, which balance the sugars they contain and help to clean the teeth. These foods also help stimulate saliva production, which washes harmful acids and food particles away from teeth and helps neutralize acid, protecting teeth from decay. Plus, many contain vitamin C (important for healthy gums and quick healing of wounds) and vitamin A (another key nutrient in building tooth enamel).

Hands down, water—particularly fluoridated water—is the most tooth-friendly beverage.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipP0VN9-Ueik4VKivEjqlNVMc6Ww8SKt7kTephJQ=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": "https://www.mgdentistry.com/", "cta_label": "Learn more", "posted_at": "2023-01-10T13:02:10", "expires_at": "2023-07-12T13:02:09", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "5465627095482056569", "text": "This 2023, be flawless, not flossless - MG Dentistry & Rejuvenation Center.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipMK6aAJOEU3eXSwgEs1dm51k7fOMvge6L_HOOYp=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2023-01-01T13:04:20", "expires_at": "2023-07-03T13:04:20", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "1774822855782885377", "text": "Hope you enjoy the Christmas eve with the ones you love and step into the new year with lots of happiness and good health. If you’ve been thinking about scheduling a dental appointment but have not gotten around to actually making the phone call, here are 5 great reasons to get yourself in gear!

1. Save money. Preventive care treatments are typically much less expensive than major restorative procedures (crowns, root canals, and dental implants). 
2. Less discomfort. From gum disease to abscessed teeth, scheduling your appointment asap is the first step towards getting the problem resolved quickly.
3. Less time away from work or school. Being proactive and scheduling your dental appointment now will give you a chance to stay ahead of your dental problems and reduce the number of additional dental visits.
4. Fewer surprises and unexpected dental emergencies. Who wants to deal with a toothache during a vacation or in the middle of the night? While some dental problems are unforeseeable, most can be prevented or addressed before they have a chance to take you by surprise.
5. More convenient appointment time. Waiting until the last minute to schedule a dental appointment often means that you’ll have to settle for any appointment time that the dentist has available. [{"id": "7230109504110049897", "text": "A Healthy Aging Check-In

Healthy Aging Month is a good reminder that changes in the mouth can reveal when an older loved one may need extra support. Use the M.O.U.T.H. checklist:

M — Meals: Are they avoiding certain foods, chewing on one side or taking longer to eat?

O — Ongoing symptoms: Watch for bleeding gums, persistent bad breath, sores, swelling or dry mouth.

U — Unusual behavior: Are they speaking less, resisting brushing or avoiding smiling and socializing?

T — Teeth and dentures: Look for loose or painful teeth, or dentures that click, slip, crack or cause sore spots.

H — Health and medications: Note changes in overall health, medications, memory, mobility or blood glucose.

If something seems different, the team at Aspen Dental can help identify the cause and recommend the right next step.

[{"id": "2475896020266319156", "text": "Bleeding gums are not something to ignore. If your gums look like they’re pulling back, feel tender, or bleed when you brush or floss, it may be time for a closer look. These can be early signs of gum disease, and in more advanced cases, bone loss around the teeth.

At American Dental, we help patients across Chicago get answers early with gentle periodontal evaluations, digital diagnostics, and clear treatment planning in a comfortable setting. If deep cleaning, also called scaling and root planing, is recommended, ongoing maintenance visits can help keep gum health stable and protect your smile over time. Regular periodontal maintenance is especially important if you’ve already had signs of inflammation, pockets, or recession.

If you’re searching for a periodontist near 60625 or want to know whether sensitive gums need treatment, our team is here to help. Don’t wait for bleeding, bad breath, or loose teeth to get worse. Request your visit with American Dental today and take the next step toward healthier gums and a stronger smile.", "type": "update", "image": null, "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-09-21T11:15:14", "expires_at": "2027-03-23T11:15:14", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "110449270969853317", "text": "Missing many or all teeth? Full-arch implant options can give you a more stable, confident smile without relying on removable dentures. At American Dental in Downtown Chicago, we use digital imaging to see whether fixed hybrid implant dentures or another implant solution is the right fit for your bone, gums, bite, and goals.

Your consultation is designed to answer the big questions clearly: Are you a candidate, how many implants may be needed, and what kind of timeline should you expect? Some patients may qualify for a temporary tooth solution while healing, while others may need a more staged approach depending on extractions, bone support, and overall oral health.

On the day of treatment, your care team will review the plan, keep you comfortable with local anesthesia, and discuss additional comfort options when appropriate. After placement, healing can take several weeks to a few months, followed by the steps needed for long-term fit, function, and appearance. Throughout the process, we focus on clear guidance, modern technology, and a comfortable experience.

If you are ready to explore a full-arch implant solution, request a consultation with our Downtown Chicago team today.", "type": "update", "image": null, "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-09-14T12:15:13", "expires_at": "2027-03-16T12:15:13", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "2744503387677376365", "text": "Labor Day is a smart time to plan the dental care you have been putting off. As fall gets busier, scheduling early can help you make the most of remaining insurance benefits and FSA funds before the year starts winding down.

At American Dental, we make it easier to stay on track with comprehensive care for the whole family, from exams and cleanings to restorative, cosmetic, orthodontic, and emergency treatment. If you have been meaning to check on a sensitive tooth, replace a filling, start aligners, or book a routine cleaning, now is a great time to get ahead of the fall rush. Our Chicago-area offices are designed for comfort, with modern digital diagnostics, clear explanations, and support with insurance questions so you can plan care with confidence.

Don’t wait until the end of the year when schedules fill up fast. Reserve your fall visit with American Dental today and take the next step toward a healthier, more confident smile.", "type": "update", "image": null, "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-09-07T12:45:14", "expires_at": "2027-03-09T12:45:13", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "5869787137821013432", "text": "Training for the Chicago Marathon or logging long bike rides this late summer? Sports drinks and energy gels can help performance, but frequent sipping can also wear down enamel and increase sensitivity.

A few smart habits can make a big difference. Try alternating with water, save acidic drinks for key training moments instead of all-day sipping, and avoid brushing right away after a sports drink. Giving your mouth a little time before brushing can help protect softened enamel. If you notice tooth sensitivity, dry mouth, or a sharp twinge with cold drinks, it may be time for a dental checkup.

At American Dental, we help Chicago-area patients stay ahead of enamel wear with gentle exams, professional cleanings, digital diagnostics, and practical guidance that fits real life. Whether you are training for race day, weekend rides, or long runs along the lakefront, our team makes dental care easy, comfortable, and accessible.

Book your visit with American Dental and keep your smile strong through training season.", "type": "update", "image": null, "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-08-31T14:30:15", "expires_at": "2027-03-02T14:30:15", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "3792749690073281987", "text": "Wondering if dental X-rays are really safe? Modern digital imaging makes them faster, more precise, and lower radiation than many patients expect. At American Dental, X-rays are recommended based on your needs, dental history, age, and current oral health, so you only get the imaging that supports accurate care.

Digital dental X-rays help us spot cavities, cracks, bone loss, infections, and other problems early, often before they become more painful, complex, or expensive to treat. That means better diagnostics, smarter treatment planning, and more confidence in your care. Our technology also allows for immediate image review right in the treatment room, so you can better understand what we see and what comes next.

Your wear schedule depends on your treatment and your bite, so it is important to follow the plan your dentist or orthodontic team gives you. [{"id": "3061434579643754168", "text": "Self-care has become a widely discussed concept, and for good reason — the demands of modern life are real, and taking deliberate time to invest in your own health and wellbeing matters. But self-care doesn't have to mean elaborate routines or significant expense. Sometimes it's as simple as booking an appointment you've been putting off.


A professional dental cleaning is, genuinely, one of the most effective things you can do for yourself in under an hour. Your hygienist removes buildup that brushing and flossing can't address, polishes away surface stains that have accumulated over months, and checks for early signs of issues that are far easier to manage now than later. You leave feeling cleaner, fresher, and with the quiet satisfaction of having done something concretely good for your health.


There's also the confidence factor. A clean, healthy smile affects how you feel in social and professional situations — it's one of the first things people notice, and taking care of it is a form of self-respect that pays dividends in ways that are hard to quantify but easy to feel.


If you've been running on fumes and putting everyone else's needs ahead of your own, this is your reminder that your health belongs on the priority list too. You can't pour from an empty cup, as the saying goes — and you can't flash a confident smile if you've been neglecting the thing that makes it possible.


Book the cleaning. You've earned it.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipPcymIX4NdOm0SiezeQvmTlUMlV8VNH7np2VAKP=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-09-18T23:00:42", "expires_at": "2027-03-20T23:00:40", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "1293393192352264113", "text": "The relationship between oral health and overall health is one of the most important — and most underappreciated — connections in medicine. For decades, dentistry and medicine operated largely in separate silos. That's changing, and the research behind the shift is compelling.


Gum disease, in particular, has been linked to a range of serious systemic conditions. The bacteria associated with periodontal infections can enter the bloodstream through inflamed gum tissue, triggering inflammatory responses throughout the body. Studies have found associations between gum disease and cardiovascular disease, stroke, type 2 diabetes, respiratory conditions, and adverse pregnancy outcomes including premature birth and low birth weight.


The relationship with diabetes is especially well established and runs in both directions. People with diabetes are more susceptible to gum disease due to impaired immune response and reduced ability to fight infection. And gum disease, in turn, can make blood sugar harder to control — creating a cycle that worsens both conditions simultaneously.


None of this is meant to be alarming. It's meant to reframe how you think about dental care. A dental visit isn't just about your teeth — it's a meaningful investment in your cardiovascular health, your metabolic health, and your overall wellbeing. Your dentist and your physician are, in a very real sense, working toward the same goal.


Take care of your gums. The rest of your body is paying attention.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipOhErftamEdsLVBmnX9T_lVnooMALuPQRc9FkOd=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-09-11T23:12:09", "expires_at": "2027-03-13T23:12:07", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "3667600773968541744", "text": "Oral health doesn't look the same at every stage of life — and for older adults, the risks and considerations shift in ways that are worth understanding. September is a good time to think about the dental health of the seniors in your life, whether that's a parent, grandparent, or yourself.

Dry mouth is one of the most common oral health challenges for older adults, and it's frequently a side effect of medications rather than aging itself. Hundreds of commonly prescribed drugs — including those for blood pressure, depression, allergies, and pain — list dry mouth as a side effect. Since saliva is the mouth's primary defense against bacteria and acid, chronically reduced saliva flow significantly increases the risk of cavities and gum disease, even in people who have maintained good oral hygiene for decades.

Gum disease is also more prevalent and more aggressive in older adults, partly due to immune system changes and partly due to accumulated exposure over time. It's the leading cause of tooth loss in adults, and tooth loss has its own downstream effects on nutrition, speech, confidence, and quality of life.

Regular dental visits are important at every age, but they're especially critical for seniors whose oral health landscape is shifting. If an older person in your life has been avoiding the dentist — whether due to cost, mobility, anxiety, or simply not prioritizing it — this is a gentle nudge to help them get back on track.
", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipOyCWcNIiqCZDI9MIa0wHP0erq6aoqPQjrrqyY1=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-09-04T23:04:46", "expires_at": "2027-03-06T23:04:44", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "8333109394098020347", "text": "September is just around the corner, and with it comes that familiar shift in pace — school routines, work schedules, and the general acceleration that carries most people straight through to the holidays before they know it. Before that happens, it's worth taking a moment to reset your oral health routine and make sure you're heading into the busier months in good shape.

Think of late August as a natural checkpoint. Have you had both of your cleanings this year? Is there any treatment your dentist has recommended that you've been putting off? Are your kids up to date on their checkups? These are easy things to let slide when life gets busy, and the fall season has a way of making everything feel more urgent and compressed.

Getting ahead of it now — before the holidays arrive and schedules become nearly impossible — means you're not scrambling in November or December trying to squeeze in appointments before the year ends and benefits reset. It also means that if any treatment is recommended, you have time to get it done while your benefits are still available.

The connection between routine and oral health is real. People who maintain consistent dental habits and keep their scheduled appointments tend to have significantly fewer and less complex dental issues over time. It's not complicated — it's just consistency.

Use this seasonal transition as your cue. A quick call to schedule your fall appointment today means one less thing to think about when September hits.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipMGJA1gLjL4VHTQGYeifyATxD7fGE91VFfTINO-=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-08-28T23:03:27", "expires_at": "2027-02-27T23:03:25", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "2494821960813418192", "text": "If you have teenagers, you're probably already aware of how central energy drinks and sports drinks have become to their daily routines. What you may not realize is just how damaging those beverages can be to their teeth — and how quickly the damage can accumulate.

The problem is twofold. Most energy drinks and sports drinks contain significant amounts of sugar, which feeds the bacteria that produce cavity-causing acid. But even the sugar-free versions are typically highly acidic on their own — with pH levels low enough to directly erode tooth enamel with repeated exposure. Enamel erosion is permanent. Once that protective outer layer is worn away, it cannot regenerate.

Teenagers are particularly vulnerable because their enamel is still maturing, and because consumption patterns tend to be high — sipping throughout the day rather than having a drink with a meal and moving on. That sustained, repeated acid exposure is far more damaging than occasional consumption would be.

The conversation worth having isn't necessarily about eliminating these drinks entirely — that's a difficult sell with most teenagers. It's about frequency and habits. Drinking through a straw reduces direct contact with teeth. Rinsing with water afterward helps neutralize acid. And avoiding these drinks as an all-day sipping habit is probably the most impactful change of all.

Bring it up at their next dental visit. Sometimes hearing it from the dentist lands differently than hearing it from a parent.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipNHPhZdVDMYbWo0cD2FaK-TN0Two7GntZRGeiel=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-08-21T23:37:58", "expires_at": "2027-02-20T23:37:56", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "3511690590271506569", "text": "A new school year is a natural reset point — new teachers, new supplies, new routines. It's also a great opportunity to revisit your child's oral health habits and make sure the basics are actually happening the way they should be.

Brushing twice a day for two full minutes is the foundation. Two minutes sounds simple, but most kids — and plenty of adults — fall well short of it without realizing. The easiest fix is a timer. A two-minute sand timer kept on the bathroom counter, a brushing app on a phone or tablet, or simply playing a favorite two-minute song can make the habit more engaging and ensure the time is actually being met.

Technique matters too. Many kids brush in fast, haphazard strokes that miss large areas entirely. Gentle, circular motions across all surfaces — outer, inner, and chewing — cover the mouth much more effectively. Make sure they're brushing their tongue as well, which harbors a significant amount of bacteria.

Flossing is equally important and even more commonly skipped. Once teeth are touching, a toothbrush simply cannot clean between them. Floss picks can be easier for kids to manage than traditional floss, and building it into the nighttime routine early makes it far more likely to stick as a lifelong habit.

Take a few minutes this week to brush alongside your kids and make sure their technique is where it should be. The habits they build now will serve them for decades.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipNOaXPkUdvjb8_oTCDOnLCZ97LHtdAHbyepgjiz=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-08-14T04:00:38", "expires_at": "2027-02-13T04:00:36", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "5825086246610208994", "text": "Here's a fact that surprises a lot of parents: tooth decay is one of the most prevalent chronic diseases among children in the United States — more common than asthma, more common than diabetes. And yet it's almost entirely preventable with the right habits and regular professional care.
Cavities don't just cause pain. They affect eating, sleeping, speaking, and concentrating. Children with untreated tooth decay miss more school, perform worse academically, and experience more disruption to their daily lives than kids whose dental health is being properly managed. The impact goes well beyond the mouth.

The encouraging part is that prevention is genuinely straightforward. Twice-daily brushing with fluoride toothpaste, daily flossing, limiting sugary snacks and beverages, drinking fluoridated water, and seeing a dentist every six months — these habits, practiced consistently, dramatically reduce a child's risk of developing cavities.

Dental sealants are another highly effective preventive tool. Applied to the chewing surfaces of back teeth, sealants create a barrier that prevents bacteria and food particles from settling into the grooves where cavities most commonly form. They're quick, painless, and can last for years.

If your child is due for a checkup, don't wait. And if cavities have been a recurring issue, ask your dentist about sealants and other preventive options. Keeping kids in the classroom starts with keeping them healthy.

", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipNY7Atd1m3p_cE-05bfPrDxrWB4Soduy_HBGL5J=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-08-07T23:22:43", "expires_at": "2027-02-06T23:22:42", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "3999597480555467392", "text": "Back to school season has a way of sneaking up fast. One minute it's the Fourth of July, and the next you're scrambling for school supplies, new shoes, and a hundred other things on the list. Before the chaos of a new school year fully takes over, there's one appointment worth getting on the calendar early — the kids' dental checkup. 


Late summer is one of the busiest times of year for pediatric dental appointments, which means if you wait too long, you'll be competing with every other family who had the same idea in August. Getting ahead of it now — while there's still flexibility in the schedule — means less stress and more appointment availability.

Beyond the logistics, there's a real health reason to prioritize it. Cavities are one of the most common chronic conditions among school-age children, and untreated tooth pain is a documented cause of missed school days and difficulty concentrating in class. A child dealing with dental discomfort isn't able to focus the way they should be. Addressing any issues before the school year starts means they're walking in on day one feeling their best.

If your child is starting at a new school this year, some programs also require proof of a recent dental exam. Check the requirements early so you're not caught off guard.

Add it to the back to school list. It's one of the most important items on it.

", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipMIJpUZnvNCqj4LRVGJ9zr3TCNegE-V-9zAolzh=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-07-31T23:45:47", "expires_at": "2027-01-30T23:45:46", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "5946358202326001554", "text": "Summer snacking is real — and between the heat, the activities, and the general abundance of treats at every backyard gathering, it's easy to fall into patterns that aren't great for your teeth. The good news is that a few simple swaps can make a meaningful difference without taking any of the fun out of the season.


The biggest issue with most popular snacks isn't just sugar — it's texture and frequency. Sticky snacks like fruit snacks, gummy candies, and granola bars cling to tooth surfaces and sit in the grooves of molars long after you've finished eating. Frequent snacking throughout the day means your teeth are under near-continuous acid attack, since oral bacteria produce acid every time they process sugar or refined carbohydrates.


Crunchy fruits and vegetables — apples, carrots, celery, cucumber — are genuinely great for your teeth. Their texture stimulates saliva production, helps scrub tooth surfaces, and most contain a high percentage of water. Cheese is another surprisingly tooth-friendly snack, as it's low in sugar, high in calcium, and helps neutralize acid in the mouth.


You don't have to give up summer treats entirely. Just be mindful of frequency — try to have sweets at mealtimes rather than throughout the day, and follow up with water.


Snack smart this summer. Your teeth are paying attention even when you're not.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipPPWJEBkUDZ2Df6g8dw_bc5omET3y61_QmGJqZv=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-07-24T23:05:12", "expires_at": "2027-01-23T23:05:11", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "6943622372894434990", "text": "Summer sports season is in full swing, and whether your kids are playing soccer, baseball, basketball, football, or any other contact or semi-contact activity, there's one piece of protective gear that's consistently overlooked — the mouthguard.


Dental injuries are among the most common sports injuries in children and adolescents. A single collision, fall, or errant elbow can result in a chipped, cracked, or knocked-out tooth — and depending on the tooth and the severity of the injury, the treatment can be complex, lengthy, and expensive. The American Dental Association estimates that mouthguards prevent hundreds of thousands of dental injuries every year.


The stock mouthguards available at sporting goods stores offer some protection, but a custom-fitted mouthguard made by your dentist offers significantly better fit, comfort, and coverage. A guard that fits properly is more likely to actually be worn — kids are far less likely to remove or avoid a guard that doesn't feel bulky or uncomfortable.


If your child is active in sports this summer and doesn't have a mouthguard, or is using a store-bought one that they complain about constantly, it's worth having a conversation with your dentist about a custom option. It's one of the most cost-effective preventive investments you can make.


Protect the smile they'll have for the rest of their life.", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipMyJKaR5u9kTrjDqF6pE4dpTCFHqirZOA5IjM3O=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-07-17T23:47:33", "expires_at": "2027-01-16T23:47:32", "promo_code": null}]

Essix retainers are clear removable retainers made using an impression of your teeth.

Drinking plenty of water throughout the day rinses away residual sugars, clears food debris, and prevents dry mouth, which naturally lowers the risk of cavity-causing acid attacks on enamel.
", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipMovdCLe37wrwso7EvHzujLm1aGqBIaBVNucN6m=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-09-21T17:59:04", "expires_at": "2027-03-23T17:59:03", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "703691431863026007", "text": "With fall sports practices underway, facial and dental injuries can happen in an instant on the field or court. Helmets and pads shield your body, but a well-fitted athletic mouthguard protects against fractured teeth, cut lips, and root damage during unexpected collisions.
", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipN0W6Oltr34NN1kLN-5_hPo1kU6R-9-wMFdO-op=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-09-18T17:58:06", "expires_at": "2027-03-20T17:58:05", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "8809545076251842975", "text": "As summer winds down and back-to-school season kicks into gear, establishing a consistent morning and night routine is key for kids. ", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipNpaEx0uPWlaX1dA_h3TytO7Xy1cwnIvHjOtztR=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-09-16T17:56:04", "expires_at": "2027-03-18T17:56:02", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "883641008300925447", "text": "When should your child have their very first dental checkup?   Dental organizations recommend scheduling a child's first visit when their first tooth erupts, or by their first birthday. Early visits help children become comfortable in the dental chair, allow us to monitor jaw development, and give parents practical guidance on brushing tiny teeth. Give your little one a great foundation for a lifetime of healthy smiles! 
", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipNLhC8-5WN7TiKwQdpbjSliQctV2bSI0TKbm2uP=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-09-14T18:26:56", "expires_at": "2027-03-16T18:26:55", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "5347038579496313839", "text": "A chipped tooth can happen in a split second on the field or court.    Athletic mouthguards cushion impacts to the face, reducing the risk of broken teeth, cut lips, and jaw injuries during contact or high-impact sports. Custom-fitted guards designed by a dentist offer superior comfort, breathing room, and protection compared to off-the-shelf options. Keep your young athlete's smile safe this season! 
", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipOQseC7Es4J5p0fJKNsJl_NQRkXs2m5rG80UtIK=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-09-09T18:21:29", "expires_at": "2027-03-11T18:21:28", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "6217109446250602835", "text": "Looking to brighten your smile for an upcoming event? While store-bought whitening strips can help with mild surface stains, professional in-office whitening uses higher-concentration bleaching agents safely applied under expert supervision. This protects your gums from irritation while delivering faster, more dramatic brightening results. Achieve a radiant, bright smile safely! 
", "type": "update", "image": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/geougc/AF1QipNwal9Q3vE1UyrKthkpXdF07t22ihkJBkSS9VcN=h400-no", "title": null, "cta_url": null, "cta_label": null, "posted_at": "2026-09-04T18:17:15", "expires_at": "2027-03-06T18:17:14", "promo_code": null}, {"id": "8385123062705724835", "text": "It’s not just candy that causes cavities—sugary drinks and frequent snacking play a major role, too! Sipping water throughout the day helps wash away lingering sugars and neutralizes acid attacks. Small nutritional tweaks protect your teeth for a lifetime.
